items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I was a good friend of Marshall's

ctx.x: So they wanted somebody to come to Europe that could fulfill the engagements and appease the impresarios. So I took the thing and I took Candy MacDonald, a drummer. It was really a whirlwind thing because I met Candy MacDonald at 12 o'clock during the day. He did not have a passport. The drums were put away for safekeeping in a pawn shop. We had to go get his drums out of pawn; go the the State Department and get a passport; I had to go to Air India and get the tickets; had to be at the airport at 7 o'clock. And…

Well, prior to that, you know, I retired right after I think '57 or '58 and, you know...I was in and out of music so much...I went up to Music Inn when Marshall Stearns had this Music Inn...they had these things, and I believe that some of the works of some of the schools in New Jersey--I think it's Rutgers--that have this New York Jazz Institute, I believe it was called. And I was a good friend of Marshall's...and I was just wondering, what ever happened to all of those tapes and things. I'm sure they had to be…
Well, I'll take a look and see. If they were taped, we should have them.
